chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Suleiman al-Hazza', from Muhammad ibn al-Fayz, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man came to him and said to him, 'My daughter has withered and she is pregnant.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What prevents you from the rice with the fat? Take four or five stones, place them by the side of the fire, and put the rice in the pot and cook it until it is done. Take the fat of fresh kidneys. When the rice is done, place the fat in a bowl along with the stones, and cover it with another bowl. Then stir it well and keep it steady so that its steam does not escape. When the fat has melted, mix it into the rice, then she can eat it.'

key_terms.الشَّحْم: fat / suet (specifically animal fat used for nourishment)

ai.seo_question: What dietary remedy did Imam al-Sadiq recommend for a weak pregnant woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical medical wisdom of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who prescribed a nutrient-dense diet of rice and fresh kidney fat to treat weakness and pregnancy-related ailments. The specific instruction to cook with stones and seal the vessel highlights an early understanding of thermal retention and steam preservation, emphasizing the holistic integration of dietary therapy (*tibb*) with spiritual guidance in Shia tradition. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how Imams addressed both physical health and maternal well-being through accessible, natural remedies.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abu Suleyman Sl Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man came over, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My daughter has withered and with her is the belly (pregnancy)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What prevents you from the rice with the fat? Take four or five stones, so place these by the side of the fire and make the rice to be in the pot and cook it until it is done, and take the fat of fresh kidneys. So when the rice reaches (is cooked), so place the fat in a bowl along with the stones, and cover over it with another bowl. Then stir it with a new stirring, and set it such that no steam comes out. So when the fat has melted, so make it to be in the rice, then she can eat it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from abu Sulayman al-Hadhddha’ from Muhammad ibn al- Fayd who has said the following:

“I once was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that a man came to him (the Imam) and said, ‘My daughter has become weak and she is pregnant.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘What prevents you from feeding her rice with fat? Take four pieces of stone or five and place them near the fire. Cook the rice in a pot until it is cooked. Take the fresh fat of a kidney. When rice is cooked then place the fat in a pot with the stones, then cover it with another pot and stir it fairly well. Fix the pots so that no steam comes out. When the fat melts; then place it in the rice, then she can eat it (ingest it).”’
